summary: Create a gzip-compressed tar archive from a source path.

file.description: Archive file to create, e.g. out.tar.gz.

from.description: Source file or directory to archive.

posix.semanticNotes: tar flags are positional/fiddly so they are emitted as literals: -czf <file> <from>. Uses gzip; the archive's stored paths are relative to the invocation cwd.

powershell.semanticNotes: DIVERGES: Compress-Archive produces a ZIP, not a gzip tar. The container format differs, so an archive produced on one platform is not byte-compatible with the other. Extraction must use the matching tool.

summary: Extract a gzip-compressed tar archive into a target directory.

posix.semanticNotes: tar -xzf <file> -C <to>. Extraction OVERWRITES existing files in `to` without prompting — hence riskDefault MEDIUM and destructive:true. A malicious archive with `../` paths can escape `to` (path traversal); validate archive contents upstream.

powershell.semanticNotes: DIVERGES: Expand-Archive only handles ZIP, not gzip tar, and ERRORS on existing files unless -Force is added (it does not overwrite by default like tar). Container format and overwrite behavior both differ.

summary: List the contents of a gzip-compressed tar archive without extracting.

powershell.semanticNotes: Uses the Windows-bundled bsdtar (`tar -tf <file>`) through the PowerShell host. This lists tar/gzip archives and, on modern Windows, ZIP archives too; exact format support depends on the installed tar.exe.
